**Rigshospitalet** is a major hospital located in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] [^src4]. It is actively monitored in the Danish national clinical quality databases, specifically the Database for Atrial Fibrillation in Denmark (Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark), which is managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1]. The hospital's performance is comprehensively evaluated across multiple clinical quality indicators for the reporting period of July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023 [^src2].

In terms of specific clinical metrics, Rigshospitalet was measured for [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]], which evaluates the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients receiving an echocardiogram [^src2]. The hospital achieved a compliance rate of 75.2% (95% CI: 71.4–78.7), which fell below the required national standard [^src2]. Furthermore, for [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]], which assesses anticoagulation treatment coverage two years post-diagnosis, Rigshospitalet again did not meet the standard, recording a proportion of 84.3% (95% CI: 78.9–88.8) [^src3]. In a 5-year analysis for the same indicator, the hospital recorded the lowest proportion among all listed hospitals at 79.7% (95% CI: 73.0–85.3) [^src4]. 

The hospital is also included in detailed hospital-level analyses for other indicators, such as Indikator 1, where it notably failed to meet the required standard [^src1]. Additional registry data tracks Rigshospitalet's performance regarding severe bleeding incidents (Indikator 7 and 12), patient education (Indikator 8), ischemic stroke (Indikator 15), intracranial hemorrhage (Indikator 14), and 1-year mortality (Indikator 13), reflecting its broad inclusion in the national cardiovascular quality monitoring framework [^src5], [^src6], [^src7].
